messages:
maya: Customer (AcmeSearch) opened a ticket: rerank API returns an error when they send ~800 short docs + a long query. They get a 413 with message 'request entity too large' and no guidance. They say this used to work in our old beta. Repro in ticket includes curl call and payload sizes. Can we triage?

sam: Thanks — can you paste the request_id / response headers from their logs? 413 implies body size limit but our reranker also enforces token-level limits after concat. Need to see if it's our fronting LB or the service.

maya: Pasted headers from customer: 
```
HTTP/1.1 413 Request Entity Too Large
x-request-id: r8b2c9f4
content-type: application/json; charset=utf-8
```
They also supplied the curl they ran: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"query":"<~1500 char query>","documents":[{"id":"d1","text":"<~4000 char>"}, ... 800 items]}'
```
They included a stack snippet from their side showing payload ~5.1MB.

julian: Right — two distinct limits are in play here: (1) the HTTP front-door (nginx) body size limit; (2) the reranker internal token budget after concatenating doc context. In practice large doc arrays blow past both. We should surface which limit triggered. The customer's response header just shows 413 so it's ambiguous.

sam: Quick triage steps: ask customer to try sending the same call but with a much smaller document list (e.g., first 50 docs) and confirm if it succeeds. If smaller succeeds, it's likely our internal enforcement or payload size. If smaller still 413, then front-door limit.

maya: Customer tried smaller (50 docs) — call succeeded but rankings looked bad because they removed relevant docs. They want to send full set then expect rerank to prioritize. So we need to: (A) provide immediate workaround and (B) improve error messaging and docs.

julian: Immediate workaround recommendation (what we told them): pre-filter candidates via embeddings (send embeddings search to limit to top 100 candidate docs), then call rerank on that subset. This reduces bytes and token count. Example flow we gave them:
```
# 1) get embeddings for query
POST /v1/embeddings
# 2) search vector index (customer side) to pick top ~100 docs
# 3) call /v1/rerank with those docs
```
Also suggested chunking long docs and/or sending batched rerank requests (e.g., 800 -> 8x requests of 100).

maya: Customer asks if we can accept a docs_count param to avoid them doing client-side filtering. They said their pipeline can't easily run a vector search before rerank.

sam: Long term we can consider server-side pre-filtering but that's a product change. Short-term UX: change 413 body to include hint text when endpoint is /v1/rerank: e.g., "Request too large for rerank. Try limiting docs, chunking long docs, or run an embeddings-enabled prefilter to <100 candidates. See docs/limits#rerank". That will cut down duplicate tickets.

katie: Create an internal ticket for docs + error message: SUP-12345. I'll add a note to update the 'limits' doc and add a code snippet for chunking/batching. Also flag for product discussion on server-side candidate filtering.

deploybot: ticket SUP-12345 created by @katie at 2026-03-17T12:34:02Z :label:triage :assignee:julian

julian: For engineering notes — current internal token budget is ~4096 effective tokens for the reranker (sum of query + concatenated snippets). That corresponds to ~3-4k words depending on encoding. If the customer's docs blow past that, we reject. Front-door nginx currently has body_max ~4MB (config). Two failure modes then.

sam: Proposed immediate change: (a) detect 413 at our front door and append a small JSON body with fields {"reason":"payload_too_large","hint":"try limiting docs to <200 or prefilter with embeddings"} before returning to customer; (b) add a structured error for token budget exceed (HTTP 400 with code "rerank_token_budget_exceeded").

maya: Customer accepted the workaround for now and will implement vector prefiltering to pass top 100. They're asking for recommended default candidate size. We told them 50-150 depending on doc length; start at 100.

julian: I'll draft the middleware change and a clear error payload. ETA for a PR: 2 working days. Will include example response and migration notes for SDKs.

katie: I'll coordinate docs update + send a short customer-facing snippet to AcmeSearch explaining the limits and recommended flow.

maya: Thanks team. I'll reply to customer with the workaround + estimated timeline for clearer errors/docs. :thumbsup:

sam: Low-priority follow-up: add a small note in the rerank error page about 'unexpected low scores' when doc truncation happens (customers sometimes misinterpret low relevance as model problem when it's actually missing context).

julian: noted. Also logging idea: include a small diagnostic header in 413 responses for internal support only (X-RW-Diag: token_budget=exceeded; bytes=5123456) so we can triage without back-and-forth. Will attach to SUP-12345.

maya: Marking action items: 1) customer: implement prefilter -> top 100 (done by customer). 2) eng: draft PR for clearer 413 middleware + structured token error (julian + sam). 3) docs: update rerank limits + example chunking pattern (katie). 4) support: follow up with customer in 48h.

katie: Adding follow-up task in Zendesk and linking SUP-12345.

maya: closing internal triage thread, will reopen if customer sees more errors. :wave:
